newsitem.title: USA: Two die in plane crash after pilot passes out.
newsitem.headline: Two die in plane crash after pilot passes out.

text.p: A teenage passenger with no flying experience took control of a small plane after the pilot passed out on Friday but she apparently also lost consciousness and both were killed when the plane crashed, authorities said.
The plane went down in a rural, wooded area near Alton, N.H., about 25 miles (40 km) northeast of Concord, after first running into trouble over Long Island Sound, more than 160 miles (250 km) away.

Air traffic controllers contacted the plane as the girl tried to take control of it over the Sound and prepared for an emergency landing at Sikorsky Airport in Stratford, Connecticut, operations manager Michael O'Donnell said.
"All we know is that he was unconscious and the other passenger in the plane was flying the plane and she had no experience," he said.
Reports said the the pilot and passenger may have been overcome by carbon monoxide fumes.
"They were about 10 miles (15 km) inbound from the airport. I guess they were going to try to get the aircraft here but they couldn't really maintain contact with the aircraft," O'Donnell said.

The single-engine plane, a four-seat Piper Cherokee Dakota, took off from at about 11:15 a.m. EST (1615 GMT) from Republic Airport in Farmingdale on Long Island, New York, airport manager Stephen Williams said.

The girl radioed to air traffic controllers about a half-hour later, O'Donnell said, but the plane continued on its flight path north, apparently on auto-pilot, across Connecticut and Massachusetts before it crashed in New Hampshire at 1:40 p.m. EST (1840 GMT).

"It's total devastation," Alton Fire Department Chief Russell Jones told reporters on the crash site. "It's not a great deal that you could recognise as a plane. It appears that it came in in an approach and then it hit a very sizeable tree and that's what did the devastation."
Pieces of the plane were strewn throughout the wooded area and the two bodies were thrown from the wreckage, eyewitnesses said.
Officials with the Federal Aviation Administration had no information on the pilot or passenger.
